thread:
Jamal (Sales Eng): Quick sync — EdgeHealth POC. Customer wants sustained 3k QPS with p50 ~100ms, p95 <250ms. They also want the ability to burst to ~12k QPS for ~2 minutes during peak windows. Security: HSM-wrapped keys + IP allowlist + SOC2 logs. Need: runbook, rough cost for sustained+burst, and any enterprise blockers.

Alex (AE): Got it. Which model variant are they testing (quantized / fp16)? pricing sensitivity?

Jamal (Sales Eng): Model is redwood-13b-q8 (quantized). Avg prompt ~38 tokens, typical response ~45 tokens, 99th token length ~420. Mostly chat traffic (90%) + occasional embedding jobs (10%). Customer flagged cost as sensitive.

Maria (SRE): We can run this on a Dedicated pool. For steady 3k QPS w/ p50 ~100ms I'd recommend baseline of 2x A100-80 GPU nodes with continuous batching + prefix caching. For safe burst to 12k we'd need warm headroom ≈ +3 GPUs. Need exact token distribution and concurrency pattern to finalize.

Rita (Solutions): Security note — they require AWS CloudHSM integration for signing, and an approval ticket for VPC endpoints/IP allowlist. Also asking for audit log retention 1 year.

Jamal (Sales Eng): Sample load script they want to run (do not run from customer-prod):
```bash
# simple single-threaded sanity loop (example)
for i in $(seq 1 1000); do
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \n    -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' \n    -d '{"model":"redwood-13b-q8","input":"summarize: ..."}' >/dev/null &
done
```

Maria (SRE): We will provide a k6 harness instead (controlled). Proposed runbook: steady-state 3k QPS for 10m, then 2m burst to 12k, then 10m cooldown. Metrics to capture: p50/p95/p99 latencies, GPU util, queue length, kernel cold-starts, KMS call latencies.

ops-bot: deploy scheduled: dedicated-pool-edge-03 -> 2026-04-05T18:00:00Z. Notify on roll completion.

Jamal (Sales Eng): Pricing question from customer: how do we bill for the 2m bursts? Do we treat as metered minutes on extra GPUs or as a separate burst rate? Need a ballpark for procurement.

Alex (AE): Short answer: baseline commit covers sustained capacity; short bursts can be metered at per-GPU-minute rate. Rough estimate: sustained 3k ≈ 0.9 GPU-equivalent (efficient batching), bursts add ~3 GPUs for 2 minutes → incremental cost ~3 * burst_rate_per_gpu_min * 2. I'll model numbers into a slide.

sec-bot: Blocking items: please upload customer SOC2 cert AND confirm CloudHSM domain (AWS CloudHSM vs other). Also require key rotation policy <= 30 days or justification.

Rita (Solutions): HSM path available in Private/Dedicated. Note: KMS/HSM crypto ops add ~8–12ms to request latency (observed), include in SLO calc.

Maria (SRE): Quick pre-run smoke results (internal): steady 3k with caching on: p50 88ms, p95 210ms, p99 410ms. During a synthetic 12k burst we saw tail spikes up to ~1.2s due to kernel cold-starts and GC pauses. Mitigations: pre-warm kernels, lower autoscale threshold, and short-lived warm instances during expected burst windows.

Jamal (Sales Eng): This is great. Can you drop a runnable runbook + cost estimate + security checklist by EOD tomorrow? Customer legal also sent standard security questionnaire — want to bundle answers.

Alex (AE): Will do. Draft runbook + cost slide link: https://share.redwood/runbooks/edgehealth-poc (internal). Sending security answers to Rita for review.

Rita (Solutions): I'll QA the sec answers and confirm CloudHSM details. If we need a signed BAA/SLA addendum, flag legal ASAP.

Maria (SRE): Action items: (1) get token distribution CSV from customer, (2) finalize harness, (3) schedule formal run and capture traces.

Jamal (Sales Eng): I'll get the CSV and legal contacts. Thanks team — pinging here when I have the file. :thumbsup:
